news.title: Kizi Apparels Limited announced that it has received INR 9.679537 million in funding from Parshva Alloys Private Limited, Evolvion Advisory Private Limited
news.body: On April 23, 2026, the company closed the transaction by closing its third and final transaction. The third tranche consists of INR 1,843,650 from individual investor Abhishek Nathani for INR 600,000, Raj Kumar Nathani for INR 495,000 and Surinder Goel for INR 748,650 on preferential basis.

news.title: Less than half of directors are independent
news.body: Following the recent departure of a director, there are only 2 independent directors on the board. The company's board is composed of: 2 independent directors. 3 non-independent directors. Non Executive & Independent Director Avani Shah was the last independent director to join the board, commencing their role in 2023. The company's minority of independent directors is a risk according to the Simply Wall St Risk Model.

news.title: Kizi Apparels Limited announced a financing transaction
news.body: Kizi Apparels Limited announced a private placement to issue 2,508,000 convertible warrants on February 12, 2026. Transaction involves participation of Abhishek Nathani for 501,000 warrant, Kiran Nathani for 399,000 warrant, Raj kumar Nathani for 300,000 warrant and other investors. The conversion can be exercised at any time during the period of 18 Months from the date of allotment Transaction is approved by board of directors and is still subject to shareholder approval. news.title: First half 2026 earnings released: EPS: ₹0.72 (vs ₹0.54 in 1H 2025)
news.body: First half 2026 results: EPS: ₹0.72 (up from ₹0.54 in 1H 2025). Revenue: ₹139.1m (up 12% from 1H 2025). Net income: ₹5.66m (up 35% from 1H 2025). Profit margin: 4.1% (up from 3.4% in 1H 2025). The increase in margin was driven by higher revenue.

news.title: New major risk - Financial position
news.body: The company's interest payments are not well covered by earnings. Net interest cover: 3.0x This is considered a major risk. If the company is unable to fund interest repayments on its debt through profits, it may be forced into reducing its debt burden through selling assets, undertaking a potentially costly capital raising or even into bankruptcy in the worst case scenario. Currently, the following risks have been identified for the company: Major Risks Interest payments are not well covered by earnings (3.0x net interest cover).
